name: org.machanism.machai:machai-mcp-server
description: Machai MCP Server is a Java 17 executable server artifact for exposing Machai GenAI functional tools and prompts through the Model Context Protocol. It acts as an MCP gateway rather than a domain-specific tool bundle: users add Machai-compatible functional tool libraries to the runtime classpath, and the server discovers, adapts, and publishes those capabilities to MCP clients. The artifact supports STDIO transport for local process-based integrations and HTTP transport for remote access, including stateless request handling and streamable session-aware communication. It is useful for AI assistant integrations, automation gateways, coding assistants, internal platform tooling, and any Java deployment that needs to make custom GenAI tools available through a standard MCP interface. The server includes command-line configuration for server name, version, project directory, port, help output, and streamable HTTP sessions. Internally it provides shared MCP server abstractions, Jetty-based HTTP hosting, STDIO server support, and adapters that convert Machai ToolFunction definitions, parameter descriptors, resources, and prompts into MCP-compliant synchronous tool specifications and results.

classification.type: executable Java library and CLI application
usageContext: Run as a command-line MCP server over STDIO for local desktop clients
Run as an HTTP MCP server for remote clients on a configured port
Use streamable HTTP sessions when MCP clients require session-aware communication
Expose custom Machai functional tools and prompts supplied by external jars on the classpath
Provide project-directory context to tools invoked by AI assistants

constructors.description: Creates an HTTP stateless MCP server that reports the supplied server name and version to MCP clients and exposes discovered Machai tools through Jetty-backed HTTP transport.

examples.description: Programmatically creates a stateless HTTP MCP server, configures a port and project directory, loads tools through a fully qualified Machai configurator variable, and starts the server for remote MCP clients.

constructors.description: Creates an HTTP streamable MCP server for session-aware MCP communication. This mode is selected by the CLI when both a port and the session option are provided.

examples.description: Programmatically starts a streamable HTTP MCP server for clients that need session-aware remote MCP access.

constructors.description: Creates the CLI entry-point class. Typical users invoke its static main method from the packaged jar rather than constructing this object directly.

examples.description: Installs the server by placing the server jar and a Machai functional tool jar on the classpath, configures HTTP mode with command-line options, and runs the executable entry point on port 45000.

features.name: main
features.signature: public static void main(java.lang.String[] args) throws java.lang.Exception
features.description: Parses CLI options and starts the appropriate MCP server transport. Without a port it starts STDIO mode. With a port it starts HTTP mode. With the session flag and a port it starts streamable HTTP mode. Options include help, name, version, projectDir, port, and session.

examples.description: Runs the server in STDIO mode for a local MCP client. Add external functional tool jars to the classpath so the server can publish usable tools.
Runs the server in streamable HTTP mode, configures project context, custom server metadata, and listens for MCP clients at the configured HTTP endpoint.

features.name: tools
features.description: Loads and registers GenAI tools with HTTP MCP server implementations by applying Machai functional tool configuration through a GenericGenaiAdapter. Registered tools become MCP tool specifications and callable handlers.

examples.description: Registers Machai functional tools from the provided fully qualified configurator object before starting the MCP server.

features.name: setProjectDir
features.description: Sets the project directory used by server tools as execution context. In HTTP mode, if no directory is configured, request-specific project-directory detection may be used when available.

examples.description: Configures a project directory so functional tools invoked through MCP can operate against a known workspace.

features.name: setPort
features.description: Configures the TCP port used by HTTP-based MCP servers before start is called.

examples.description: Sets the HTTP listener port for a streamable MCP server deployment.

customizations.name: External Machai functional tool jars
customizations.description: The server is intentionally extensible through additional jars that implement Machai functional tools and prompts. Put those jars on the runtime classpath with the server jar so the tool loader can discover and publish them through MCP.

examples.description: Starts the MCP server with a custom functional tool container jar so clients can discover and invoke those tools.

studs.name: org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.AbstractMcpServer
studs.description: Base implementation for MCP servers. It provides common working-directory management and shared hooks for concrete STDIO and HTTP server implementations.

studs.name: org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.AbstractHttpMcpServer
studs.description: Base class for HTTP MCP server implementations. It provides Jetty server setup, thread pool management, port configuration, and servlet transport provider registration.

examples.title: Install and run in STDIO mode
steps: Download machai-mcp-server.jar from the release distribution or build it with mvn clean package.
Prepare at least one Machai-compatible functional tool jar and place it on the Java classpath.
Configure your local MCP client to launch the same command over standard input/output.
examples.description: Use this scenario for desktop clients that communicate with MCP servers by starting a local process.

examples.title: Install, configure, and run as a remote HTTP MCP server
steps: Build the packaged jar with mvn -Ppack install or download a release jar.
Add the server jar and functional tool jars to the classpath.
Export any environment variables required by loaded tools, such as gw_model, embedding_model, GENAI_USERNAME, and GENAI_PASSWORD.
Connect an MCP client to http://localhost:45000/mcp.
examples.description: Use this scenario when multiple clients or remote clients need access to the published Machai tools through HTTP.

examples.title: Configure Claude Desktop for STDIO
examples.description: Configure Claude Desktop to launch the server locally. The server publishes tools discovered from jars on the configured classpath.
